key_insight: Axion makes finite element fracture simulations differentiable and GPU-native by compiling the full solution workflow into one on-device JAX program.
engineering_relevance: Faster fracture analysis and solution sensitivities could support parameter calibration and design studies for complex structures and materials.
method: JAX/XLA compiles element kernels, nonlinear solves, damage updates, and load stepping for GPU execution.
Automatic differentiation provides consistent element tangents and solution sensitivities.
Matrix-free operators, fixed-array octree refinement, and domain decomposition support large-scale and multi-GPU simulations.
evidence_signal: On the 2D benchmark at identical discretization, one GPU achieved 37.9× speedup over FEniCSx on one CPU; four-GPU strong and weak scaling efficiencies were 92% and 96%, with a 96M-DOF dam demonstration on one GPU.
watch_item: The reported speedup compares different hardware, and the abstract does not quantify sensitivity accuracy or differentiation cost through bound-constrained fracture solves.
paper_title: Axion: A differentiable, GPU-native finite element framework,demonstrated on phase-field fracture
